adjudication_rationale: It reports only a general majority pattern and two examples, omitting the other improvements and the XNLI and Lambada decreases.
General near-equivalence does not report the ties, MeanEmbed MMLU ordering, or the Belebele and WikiText advantages.
It reports the absence of statistical tests but omits the single-evaluation design and unavailable standard errors.
The passage reports weaker out-of-domain shortening, but not the out-of-domain relative accuracies that are part of this mixed transfer finding.
“All same-generator comparisons” covers Llama3 against both baselines on both datasets; the ChatGPT comparison establishes that Llama3 also has each dataset’s highest T1 mean.
The passage reports the central 2x finding: significant fine-tuned-over-NFT gains across all four dataset/generator settings. The stability pattern is supplementary detail.
The passage gives selected comparisons but does not report e5 outperforming every Model M variant across all four metrics or the Recall@200 near-tie.
It reports the absence of significance testing, but not that sparse or incomplete judgments make recall-based transfer results unreliable.
It reports some baseline-specific variation, but omits Model M-40M’s weakness, size dependence, Recall@200 comparisons, and gte-modernbert-base’s failure.
It accurately communicates mixed content performance and qualifies the comparison as applying to most baselines; omitting Claude’s specific exception does not reverse that finding.
The edit variant is characterized relative to the beam variant, not vanilla LLaMa-3-8B, so the required mixed comparison is not reported.
It reports the single-run scope, absence of significance tests, and consequent descriptive status; omitted human-evaluation details do not alter that limitation.
It reports e5 superiority for MRR@100 and NDCG@100 only, omitting both recall comparisons and the 0.001 Recall@200 margin.
The passage lists Method M’s p-values for all four named benchmarks; each is below 0.001 and is interpreted as membership evidence.
It correctly reports lower full-method p-values, but omits the contrasting across-benchmark significance patterns of the two ablations, an essential part of the mixed finding.
The complete benchmark-level p-values encode the reported significance pattern for PaCoST, both LLM DI variants, and Method M.
The passage mentions small significant effects for medical roles, but does not report significance for every persona or the effect-size separation and robot exception.
It reports Method M+ versus CERT-ED but omits Method M’s lower Yelp and higher SpamAssassin/LUN cardinalities, materially under-covering the finding’s entities and scope.
It mentions Method M’s disadvantage only on Yelp and LUN, omitting SpamAssassin and the finding that Method M+ was below CERT-ED on every dataset.
It incorrectly describes WikiText superiority as a higher score and omits three of the six accuracy benchmarks.
It reports only a general majority pattern and two examples, without identifying the five improvements or two decreases.
It claims Method M was higher than the simple methods on 1B MMLU and GSM8K, where it tied or was slightly lower.
The no-tests limitation is reported, but the single evaluation and missing-standard-error limitations are absent.
It correctly compares Method M with CERT-ED across all datasets but omits the required finding that Method M also exceeded RanMASK on all three.
“Did not consistently outperform” understates the universal result: both Method M and M+ had lower clean accuracy than CERT-ED on every dataset.
The passage gives only a majority summary, without reporting the four specific wins or FOCUS’s GSM8K advantage.
It illustrates MMLU and WikiText but omits the ARC-C and GSM8K ties and the Belebele advantage.
It describes an ARC-C gap although ARC-C was preserved exactly, and it omits the Belebele decline.
It notes that tests were absent but does not report the single evaluation or unavailable standard errors.
The passage correctly shows inconsistency but wrongly calls HotpotQA/BGE exact match a loss; Method M tied PDist at 60.9.
“Did not consistently outperform” understates the universal result and provides only Yelp evidence; both methods were below CERT-ED on all three datasets.
The three displayed losses are reported accurately, but calling them the three evaluated losses incorrectly excludes four additional paired losses with positive average gains.
It correctly notes the GPT-2 setting and absent significance tests, but falsely limits testing to three losses and omits other stated evidential limitations.
The displayed gains are accurate, but “three evaluated KD losses” understates scope because four additional paired losses also had positive average gains.
The passage correctly identifies GPT-2-only evidence and absent significance tests, but incorrectly says only three losses were tested and incompletely characterizes the limitations.
It covers three metrics but omits Recall@200, including the important result that Model M-110M trailed e5 by only 0.001.
It characterizes transfer as non-generalizing against the best baseline, obscuring the mixed baseline-specific results and omitting size dependence and gte-modernbert-base’s failure.
The separately reported ZeroGen and 1x NFT values establish negative/tied Llama3 effects and positive Zephyr effects, supporting the stated dependence pattern.
It explicitly reports fine-tuned superiority over NFT in all four 2x settings and the significance markings; examples also show the stated volume-change behavior.
It omits BN and conflates variants on MR: M-static decreased MR BLEU, while only M-dynamic improved it slightly.
The unqualified statement that no significance tests were reported correctly conveys that statistical reliability was not established, despite omitting seed and standard-deviation details.
It correctly covers MMLU, ARC-C, GSM8K, and WikiText but omits Method M’s worse Belebele performance.
It reports the overall mixed result but reverses one comparison: Gemma MMLU for Method M (39.18%) was below Rand (39.73%), not above it.
It implies wins across all RankT5 datasets but wrongly identifies the largest gain: Musique improved by 0.4 points, versus HotpotQA’s 0.3.
The aggregate “matched or exceeded” claim does not report that HotpotQA/BGE was a tie and Musique/BGE an outright win.
It reports only the medical-role subset under alternative embeddings, omitting that all personas were significant and that effect sizes separate roles except for the robot.
The reported gains for GKD, KLD, and SRKL are correct, but describing these as all evaluated losses excludes four additional paired losses reported in the note.
It accurately conveys the central evidence limits: GPT-2-only included results, five evaluation sets, and no standard deviations or statistical tests; omitted details do not contradict this.
It correctly communicates non-uniform superiority by reporting Llama’s round-3 deficit, Llama’s round-5 lead, and Gemma’s leads; omitting the additional round-4 deficit does not reverse the finding.
All four Method M p-values are explicitly listed, are below 0.001, and concern the intentionally contaminated benchmarks.
The passage reports full Method M outperforming both ablations, but omits their materially different significance patterns across the four benchmarks.
The complete ordered p-value comparisons across all benchmarks establish exactly which baseline variants crossed 0.05 and that Method M did so throughout.
“BLEU gains were mixed” does not report the language-specific directions or distinguish the static and dynamic variants required by the finding.
The passage correctly reports M-dynamic’s DE and ZH gains but omits the contrasting mixed high-resource results for M-static.
The comparison reports increases for only BLEU, COMET-KIWI, and XCOMET; it does not report the COMET increase or that all four metrics increased.
All same-generator comparisons include Llama3 against ZeroGen and SuperGen; the open-generator comparison with ChatGPT completes Llama3’s highest-mean status on both datasets.
Baseline comparisons are correctly described as untested, but claiming no statistical test for 2x contradicts T2, where ** denotes the reported one-tailed paired t-test.
The passage covers the transfer-length results but omits both out-of-domain relative accuracy results, so the full mixed finding is not reported.
The passage gives only a most-benchmarks significance summary; it neither states nor supplies enough baseline values to establish every method-by-benchmark comparison.
It correctly concludes that unseen data were not flagged in either setting; the misstated held-out minimum remains above 0.05 and does not change that finding.
It reports only the broad majority pattern and collapses the baselines, omitting the distinct PaCoST and two LLM DI significance patterns required by the finding.
Although relevant values appear across the passage, the edit variant’s mixed performance relative to vanilla LLaMa-3-8B is never stated.
The passage reports structural non-improvement and reduced ROUGE-L but omits the countervailing FactCC increase, so the specified mixed finding is not fully reported.
It explicitly shows a mixed trade-off: lower ROUGE-L but higher FactCC and AlignScore against the named comparators; omitted broader comparisons do not contradict this.
The passage describes the edit variant and concludes that beam is better, but never reports the required edit-versus-vanilla comparison.
The reported ZeroGen and 1x NFT values jointly show Llama3 below/tied and Zephyr above ZeroGen, establishing the mixed fine-tuning-dependence finding.
It explicitly states that at 2x fine-tuning beats NFT in all four combinations with significance; reported examples also illustrate stable/rising fine-tuned performance and mixed NFT behavior.
The passage reports M-dynamic’s high-resource gains correctly but omits M-static’s decreases on DE and marginal ZH differences.
It reports lower values without FILTER/NN for three metrics but omits COMET, so the finding that all four metrics increased is not fully reported.
The passage does not state universal lower p-values or provide sufficient PaCoST and LLM DI values to establish every comparison across all four benchmarks.
It identifies LLM DI-different’s two detections but understates entity-specific results, omitting PaCoST’s TriviaQA detection and LLM DI-same’s complete failure.
Although not verbally juxtaposed, the quoted ZeroGen and NFT values directly establish both Llama3’s absent gain and Zephyr’s retained gain.
The passage directly reports fine-tuned superiority over NFT across all four 2x combinations and significance; its examples support the associated volume-change pattern.
The aggregate better-preservation claim does not report superiority on all six accuracy benchmarks and lower WikiText bits per byte.
It reports only improvements on most metrics with two examples, omitting the complete improvement pattern and both decreases.
The across-settings superiority claim misstates the 1B simple-baseline comparison, which contains ties and a slight MMLU disadvantage.
Only the absence of statistical tests is stated; the single evaluation and missing standard errors are not reported.
